AVALON CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  TUESDAY, MARCH 17, 2026— 5:00 PM
  410 AVALON CANYON ROAD, AVALON, CA 90704
  AGENDA

In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting,
please contact the City Clerk’s Office (310) 510-0220. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City
to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35.104 ADA Title II). All
public records relating to an agenda item on this agenda are available for the public inspection at the time the records
are distributed to all, or a majority of all, members of the City Council. Such records shall be available at City Hall
located at 410 Avalon Canyon Rd.

 For the public’s convenience, but not participation, the meeting can be viewed:
  On local cable: Catalina Broadband Solutions channel 3
  Streaming on YouTube: https :/!www.youtube.com/CityofAvalonCA

CITY MANAGER REPORT I CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS I REQUESTS I MAYOR REPORT

ORAL COMMUNICATION
Members of the public may address the City Council at this time. No action will be taken on
non-agenda items at this meeting. Speakers should limit comments to two (2) minutes each.

PUBLIC HEARING

1.  TDA Article 8 Hearing
  The Metropolitan Transit Authority (MTA) is required to hold a public hearing on the
  community’s unmet public transit needs in accordance with the Transportation
  Development Act (TDA) Article 8. TDA Article 8 funds are currently being used by the City
  of Avalon to fund Avalon’s Consolidated Land Transportation Program which includes
  DAR and fixed routes.
  Recommended Action
  Open the Public Hearing and accept comments from the public. Close the Public Hearing.

PRESENTATIONS

2.  Presentation by the Salvation Army Long Beach Red Shield’s Captain Jared Arnold on
  the ongoing Partnership with City of Avalon’s Community Services Department. (10
  minutes)

3.  Bryan Barcena, Curator-at-Large for Los Angeles Nomadic Division, will introduce a
  large-scale, public art project taking place on the island from May to October 2027. (10
  minutes)

4.  Gail Fornasiere of Catalina Island Health will provide an update regarding Catalina
  Island Health. (10 minutes)

CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  City Council Minutes
  Although the live recording is the official record of public meetings, minutes are prepared
  for the City Council’s approval.
  Recommended Action
  Approve minutes from March 3, 2026 regular City Council Meeting.

6.  Warrants
  Expenditures Submitted for Approval:
  • Warrants totaling $2,177,236.74.
  • One payroll totaling $262,097.57.
  • Two electronic fund transfers totaling $111,461.88.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the disbursements for February 9, 2026 through February 27, 2026 totaling
  $2,550,796.19.

7.  Amendments to 2026 Waterside Permits Renewal List
  On January 20, 2026, the City Council approved Waterside Permit renewals for 2026.
  The Harbor Department discovered errors in the renewal list. City Staff recommends the
  list approved on January 20 be rescinded and replaced to accurately reflect the waterside
  permit renewals for 2026.
  Recommended Action
  Rescind and replace the waterside permit renewal list for 2026.

8.  Civic Center Housing Project Phase 3B Bid Results
  In October 2025, City staff published two Civic Center Housing requests for proposal for
  on-site civil preparation work (Phase 3A) and for modular unit construction (Phase 3B).
  On February 19, 2026, the City received one bid from US-Offsite. After review of the bid
  package, it was deemed incomplete and nonresponsive as the City did not receive a
  required bid bond for the project.
  Recommended Action
  1. Reject received bid as nonresponsive. 2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to
  re-scope and re-bid the project per Public Contracts Code 22038(a).
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 17, 2026
PAGE 3

GENERAL BUSINESS

9.  2025 General Plan Housing Element Annual Progress Report
  Government Code §65400 mandates each elected board submit an annual progress
  report (APR) to the California Department of Housing and Community Development
  (HCD) and the Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation (LCI) on the status
  and progress of the City’s Housing Element implementation.
  Recommended Action
  Receive and file the General Plan Housing Element Annual Report for 2025 and direct
  staff to submit the Housing Element Annual Progress Report to the California Department
  of Housing and Community Development and the Governor’s Office of Lane Use and
  Climate Innovation.

10.  Electric Vessel Charging Infrastructure at Avalon Harbor
  In 2024, the Avalon Harbor Department applied for and was awarded a CORE Voucher
  from the State of California’s Clean Off-Road Equipment (CORE) Program. The CORE
  Program is designed to subsidize the adoption of zero-emission commercial harbor craft.
  As an additional benefit of the program, the City received a voucher for $75,000 to offset
  the cost to establish a shore power resource <99kW.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make an affirmative finding to dispense with a competitive procurement process due
  to economic efficiency as outlined in Avalon Municipal Code 3-4.111(c). 2. Authorize the
  City Manager to negotiate the purchase and installation of a marine electric vessel
  charger with Aqua superPower.

11.  Civic Center Housing Project Phase 3A Bid Results
  In October 2025, the City published two Civic Center Housing requests for proposal for
  on-site civil preparation work (Phase 3A) and for modular unit construction (Phase 3B).
  The City received one bid package from Jordahi Construction, Inc. totaling $1,731,490
  which exceeds project budgeting projections.
  Recommended Action
  Pursuant to Public Contract Code Section 20167: 1. Reject all bids received for the Civic
  Center Housing Phase 3A: Site Preparation Project; 2. Adopt a resolution by a four-fifths
  vote declaring the project can be performed more economically by day labor, or materials
  or supplies furnished at a lower price in the open market; 3. Authorize the City Manager
  or designee to negotiate a revised contract scope with Jordahi Construction, Inc. for the
  Civic Center Housing Project Phase 3A: Site Preparation and return to City Council for
  final award.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 17, 2026
PAGE 4

12.  Setting a Public Hearing Date for the Proposed Rate Changes to the Sewer, Salt Water,
  and Solid Waste Service Fees
  At the March 3, 2026, City Council Meeting, HDR Engineering presented the results of
  the cost of service study. It was recommended that the City establish maximum rates for
  the sewer, saltwater, and sold waste service fees sufficient to fund the operations and
  crucial infrastructure improvements for the next five years, while maintaining adequate
  reserves. The adopted rates in future years will be reviewed annually and may be lowered
  (not increased) or held in abeyance without an additional Prop 218 process.
  Recommended Action
  1. Discuss and provide direction to Staff regarding the fees for the Sewer, Saltwater, and
  Solid Waste services. These property-related fees can only be increased by a four-fifths
  vote of the City Council. 2. Set a public hearing for May 19, 2026 for the City Council to
  hear public comments on the annual sewer, saltwater, and solid waste fees.

13.  Advance Payment of Measure C Funds to the Catalina Island Medical Center (CIMC)
  On March 6, 2025, the CIMC asked the City to approve execution of a non-binding letter
  of interest for a potential advance payment of approximately $2.93 million from the City’s
  general fund so that CIMC can participate in a program to receive a substantial increase
  in funding specifically, the Voluntary Rate Range Intergovernmental Transfer (IGT)
  -

  Program. The advance would be paid back over the course of several years through any
  available CIMC revenues, including Measure C funds.
  Recommended Action
  Provide direction on whether to enter into the letter of interest which could lead to an
  agreement wherein the City advances approximately $2,927,441.90 for CIMC’s
  participation in the Voluntary Rate Range Intergovernmental Transfer Program, which
  CIMC believes will result in increased funding for CIMC. The City would be paid back
  through any available CIMC revenues, including Measure C funds, over the course of
  several years.

ADJOURN

NOTICE OF POSTING

I, Devin Elise Hart, declare that the City Council Agenda for Tuesday, March 17, 2026 was
posted on Friday, March 13, 2026 on the City’s website, www.cityofavalon.gov/agendacenter,
and at City Hall, 410 Avalon Canyon Road.

Devin Elise Hart, Senior Management Analyst

4.  Appeal of Commercial Vehicle Permit
  1. Mayor Marshall opened the Public Hearing. 2. No Public Comments were heard.
  3. Mayor Marshall closed the Public Hearing. 4. City Council considered the

  Officer and refund the appeal fee.
  Councilmember Lavelle recused herself due to a potential conflict of interest.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Mary Schickling.

GENERAL BUSINESS

5.  Repairs to Engine 7
  Per the City’s procurement policy, City Council authorized the City Manager or
  designee, to execute an agreement with Performance Truck Repair in Azusa, CA,
  to perform essential repairs to Fire Department Engine 7 for a not-to-exceed sum
  of $30,000.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Michael Ponce. (All Ayes)

6.  Authorize Filing of a Civil Complaint for Nuisance Abatement and Appointment of
  a Receiver for 343 Sumner Avenue
  City Council authorized the filing of a civil complaint for nuisance abatement and
  filing a petition for the appointment of a receiver for the real property at 343 Sumner
  Avenue, Avalon CA 90704 based on nuisance conditions resulting from health and
  safety violations of the Avalon Municipal Code.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Mary Shickling.
  (All Ayes)

SUBJECT:  Civic Center Housing Project Phase 3B Bid Results

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1.) Reject received bid as nonresponsive. 2.) Authorize the City
Manager or designee to re-scope and re-bid the project per Public Contracts Code 22038(a).

REPORT SUMMARY: On October 7, 2025 City Council authorized City staff to publish two Civic
Center Housing requests for proposal (REP) for on-site civil preparation work (Phase 3A) and
for modular unit construction (Phase 3B).

On December 15, 2025, the City published the REP for the Civic Center Housing Project Phase
3B, which closed on February 19, 2026. The City received one bid package from US-Offsite (the
same company awarded the agreement for procurement of the manufactured units) for $4,041,
089.

After review of the single bid package, it was deemed incomplete and nonresponsive as the City
did not receive a required bid bond for the project.

Applicable to the City, PCC 22038(a) in relevant part states: If after the first invitation of bids all
bids are rejected, after reevaluating its cost estimates of the project, the public agency shall have
the option of the following: (1) Abandoning the project or readvertising for bids in the manner
described by this article.

Therefore, City Staff requests that City Council authorize the City Manager to further refine the
scope of the project and re-bid. During further investigation it was determined there are entities
interested in the logistics (moving the units from the manufacturing facility to Avalon, and
stitching the units together on site) versus general contractor work (roofing, stairs, siding,
finishing work). If approved by Council, City staff will create these separate procurement
packages and re-bid. This will result in creating bid packages Phase 3B and Phase 3C.

A final recommendation on whether to proceed with the project, as well as a final contract award
(if approved) will be provided to the City Council for authorization at a later date.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Improve local housing.
 FISCAL IMPACTS: There is $2,000,000 allocated in Capital Project 205014 Civic Center
Housing Project for FY2025-26. City staff will return to City Council with further funding and
financing recommendations before proceeding with Phase 2 and Phase 3.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Discuss and provide direction to Staff regarding the fees for
the Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste services. These property-related fees can only be
increased by a four-fifths vote of the City Council. 2. Set a public hearing for May 19, 2026 for
the City Council to hear public comments on the annual sewer, saltwater, and solid waste fees.

REPORT SUMMARY: At the March 3, 2026, HDR Engineering presented the results of the
cost of service study. It was recommended that the City establish maximum rates for the
sewer, saltwater, and sold waste service fees sufficient to fund the operations and crucial
infrastructure improvements for the next five years, while maintaining adequate reserves. The
adopted rates in future years will be reviewed annually and may be lowered (not increased) or
held in abeyance without an additional Prop 218 process.

Proposition 218 and the Next Steps

The Sewer, Salt Water, and Solid Waste Funds are enterprise funds for which a fee is charged
in exchange for the cost of service. These funds are intended to support themselves by
collecting sufficient revenues to cover the cost of service. The process of increasing rates of
the City’s sewer, salt water and solid waste service fees is subject to the 1996 constitutional
amendment known as “Proposition 218, Right to Vote on Taxes Act.” Sewer, salt water, and
solid waste service fees may be adopted five years in advance.

The main requirements of Proposition 218 are:

  •  Rates must be based on the actual cost of service;
  •  The City must mail a notice to all affected property owners of the proposed change in
  rates and public hearing;
  •  The City must hold a public hearing at least 45 days after the mailing of the notices;
  •  Proposed change in rates is considered rejected if written protests are received from a
  majority of the affected property owners; or
  •  Rates can become effective 30 days after the public hearing and adoption of an
  ordinance.

Staff will mail notices of the public hearing to all parcel owners and advertise the public hearing
in the local newspaper and the City’s web site. The published rates in the notices will be the
same as the rates presented at the March 3, 2026 City Council Meeting.

On July 24, 2025, the City Council approved the City to enter into an Voluntary Rate Range

An explanation of the program and structure of the potential arrangement is discussed below.

BACKGROUND: The Medicaid program (called “Medi-Cal” in California) is jointly funded by the
State of California and the federal government for certain residents of the State. The State’s
share of the funding is a combination of State funds appropriated to the DHCS, public funds
transferred from other public agencies such as cities or counties (called “Intergovernmental
Transfer” or “IGT”), and certain health care-related taxes. These funds together represent the
“non-federal share” of the funding to pay for Medi-Cal program expenses and are used to draw
down matching federal funds.

 The amount of federal funds available depends on the “federal matching assistance percentage”

Federal Medicaid managed care rules permit DHCS to annually develop and certify a range of
actuarially sound capitation rates that it will pay to each of contracted Medi-Cal managed care
plans, which must be reviewed and approved each year by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid
Services in order to be eligible for federal matching funds.

There is a special program that CIMC wants to participate in to obtain increased funding for its
services. Specifically, the Voluntary Rate Range Intergovernmental Transfer Program was
established in 20 11-2012 to allow local public “transferring entities” to contribute their own funds
via IGTs to help DHCS to pay capitation rates to Medi-Cal managed care plans at the upper
bound of the rate range and to draw down matching federal funds based on those higher rates.
The plans must use the “rate range increases” (that is, the difference between the lower bound
and the upper bound of the range) to make increased payments to health care providers to
increase access to services for their Medi-Cal enrollees.

Participation in the program is voluntary for public transferring entities and each Medi-Cal
managed care plan. For each Medicaid managed care plan year (calendar year), DHCS asks
the managed care plans and transferring entities for their interest in participating in the
Program—demonstrated by completing a non-binding Letter of Interest (“LOI”)—and for
information on the uncompensated care costs for the Medi-Cal enrollees in their plan.

CIMC is asking the City of Avalon to use unallocated funds from the City’s General Fund to
support CIMC’s participation in the Voluntary Rate Range Program with L.A. Care. L.A. Care is
one of the three Medi-Cal managed care plans that covers Medi-Cal members in Los Angeles
County. Most of the Medi-Cal patients who receive services at CIMC are enrolled in L.A. Care.
If approved by the City Council, the City would sign and submit the attached non-binding LOIs
included as Attachment A and the attestations included as Attachment B to L.A. Care and
HealthNet in order to demonstrate its interest in participating in the program. L.A. Care must
submit these documents on behalf of all transferring entities to DHCS by April 10, 2026.

members and cannot be used to pay back the City. The City is expected to be paid back primarily
from the use of funds from Measure C, the sales tax that was approved by City voters for support
of hospital services, as well as other available CIMC revenues. Revenue and Taxation Code
sections 7286.25-7286.26 authorize Avalon to impose a special sales tax to be used “exclusively
for the Avalon Municipal Hospital and Clinic.” This authority is broad and seems to contemplate
that the Hospital could use Measure C funds to repay debt incurred for the benefit of the Avalon

CIMC is seeking to participate in the program as it faces an ongoing structural deficit largely due
